title: Two norms on C([0,1])
promptMarkdown:
On $C([0,1])$ consider the sup norm $\|f\|_\infty=\sup_{x\in[0,1]}|f(x)|$ and the integral norm $\|f\|_1=\int_0^1|f(x)|\,dx$. Let $f_n(x)=x^n$ for $n\ge 1$.

1. Compute $\|f_n\|_\infty$ and $\|f_n\|_1$ for general $n$, with justification.
2. Decide whether there is a constant $C>0$ such that $\|f\|_\infty\le C\,\|f\|_1$ for every $f\in C([0,1])$. Prove your answer.
3. Explain in one or two sentences what this shows about equivalence of norms, and name the hypothesis of the finite-dimensional theorem that fails here.
hintLadder: Where on $[0,1]$ does $x^n$ take its largest value, and what is that value?
Compute $\int_0^1 x^n\,dx$ exactly for a general $n$; do not stop at particular values of $n$.
Suppose a single constant $C$ worked for every continuous $f$. Apply the inequality to $f_n$ and look at what happens as $n\to\infty$.
The theorem that all norms are equivalent has a hypothesis about the dimension of the space. Which of Example 6's facts about $C([0,1])$ is relevant?
